summary: Today’s pulse tracks White House restores access to media outlets banned by Trump after judge's order, Netanyahu’s speech at UN spurs protests in New York City: ‘Let Gaza live’, and Journalists for CNN, MS Now and Politico allowed back into the White House after judge’s ruling. Across BBC and Guardian, the strongest repeated signals are house, white, and journalists. headlines.title: White House restores access to media outlets banned by Trump after judge's order
headlines.description: CNN, Politico and MS NOW were allowed back into the White House after some of their staff were earlier turned away.

headlines.title: Netanyahu’s speech at UN spurs protests in New York City: ‘Let Gaza live’
headlines.description: Protest outside UN headquarters drew hundreds of people as Israeli prime minister prepared to speak As the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu , prepared to deliver his speech at the UN headquarters in New York City on Thursday, hundreds of people blocked traffic on the streets outside, with several people arrested as of early afternoon. The protest outside the UN, one of several this week against the embattled Israeli leader, drew hundreds of Jewish, Palestinian, Iranian and Lebanese New Yorkers, among others, as well as several elected officials and candidates in the November election, and a number of celebrities.

headlines.title: Journalists for CNN, MS Now and Politico allowed back into the White House after judge’s ruling
headlines.description: The outlets had requested an emergency hearing after the White House initially seemed to flout a judge’s order US politics live – latest updates Journalists for CNN, MS Now and Politico were finally granted access to the White House on Thursday afternoon, many hours after a federal judge had ruled that the Trump administration must allow them back in after imposing a ban. Earlier attempts by the journalists to enter the building had been unsuccessful, and lawyers representing the three organizations had told a judge that the White House has already “repeatedly violated” his overnight order requiring the Trump administration to return the press badges of journalists from the three news organizations.

headlines.title: Journalists from CNN, Politico, and MS Now belatedly regain access to White House after judge ruling – live
headlines.description: A federal judge had ruled Trump administration must immediately return the outlets’ press passes and said ban likely unconstitutional “This morning journalists from each of CNN, MS NOW, and POLITICO attempted to enter the White House and were turned away, and Secret Service agents confiscated the hard pass of journalists whose hard passes had not previously been confiscated,” a new court filing read.

headlines.title: US citizen injured after ICE agents reportedly mistook him for fugitive
headlines.description: Man left bloodied and hurt after immigration enforcement agents tried to arrest him in Evanston, a Chicago suburb An eyewitness has described how two federal immigration agents allegedly beat and badly injured a US citizen in a botched arrest attempt in Illinois , and left the man dazed and bleeding on the ground as they walked away after realizing their apparent mistake. Bystander Ryan Garton told the Associated Press that he saw the agents pinning down the man, who is Black, on the side of the road as he was driving home on Sunday in Evanston, a suburb of Chicago. He said he pulled over to record what was happening on video.

headlines.title: Police arrest far-right activist Daniel Thomas after ‘dinghy slashed in Channel’
headlines.description: Thirty-seven-year-old in custody on suspicion of crimes including criminal damage with intent to endanger life The far-right agitator and anti-migrant activist Daniel Thomas has been arrested on suspicion of criminal damage with intent to endanger life after he filmed himself appearing to slash the side of a dinghy in the middle of the Channel while a rescuer was onboard. The arrest came as the Home Office recorded 781 arrivals in 10 boats on Wednesday, the highest number for a single day so far this year. Responding to the figures, the government said it would “push further and harder” to crack down on the people organising the crossings.

headlinePool.title: Greek PM urges UK PM to return Elgin Marbles permanently
headlinePool.description: Andy Burnham said in 2023 the sculptures should be returned to Greece with "no strings attached".

headlinePool.title: US mortgage rates top 7% for first time in 20 months
headlinePool.description: Increase comes after Fed decision to raise interest rates, as Americans struggle with high prices and stagnant wages US mortgage rates surpassed 7% for the first time since January 2025, according to federal lender Freddie Mac, aggravating a housing market that has endured years of high interest rates and low supply. The increase comes after the US Federal Reserve hiked interest rates , which directly affect mortgage rates, for the first time since 2023, citing high inflation.

headlinePool.title: Londoners get £3bn a year subsidy because structure of council tax biased against north, says thinktank – UK politics live
headlinePool.description: Resolution Foundation says households outside London are paying hundreds of pounds a year more in council tax than they would be under a fair system Tim Shipman has written about what will be coming up at the Labour conference next week in his cover story for the Spectator. He says: Labour special advisers summoned last week to the pillared state room on the first floor of No. 10 to hear the plan for conference from Burnham’s political secretary, Hayden Munro, left in no doubt that the PM wants to be a transformational figure. The conference ‘narrative’ these advisers were urged to push includes the telling line: ‘This Labour government will bring forward the biggest change to Britain in 40 years, with a new political and economic model.’ On the specifics, Burnham will pledge: ‘We will make the choices that are needed to end rough sleeping, solve the social care crisis and get more young people into work.’ Burnham will pledge to run a ‘cost-of-living government’ with further ‘immediate action’ to ‘provide the breathing space people need’, as well as outline plans to devolve power ‘out of Whitehall’, ‘reindustrialise Britain’ and take back public control of ‘the essentials in life – such as energy, water and housing’ to ‘make them affordable again’. Ultimately, the election choice is Burnham’s. ‘If you knew what Keir’s aides thought, you knew what he would do,’ says a ministerial aide. ‘But Andy has political opinions of his own.’ Burnham may go for it. But those closest to him doubt it. ‘He likes risk, but he has stuff he wants to get done,’ says one close confidant. While outsiders think his ambitions require an election, Burnham thinks he can transform Britain without one. ‘Andy really cares about the devolution stuff,’ the ministerial aide observes. ‘Most of Westminster roll their eyes but he thinks that will change the country. He thinks doing that will make him a great prime minister.’ And those who think none of that will deal with Britain’s economic problems seize on another clue. A Labour adviser concludes: ‘Ultimately I think Burnham and his team will do what they often do with difficult decisions, and not make one.’ What I imagine is that some schools will offer some of these subjects where their local labour market demands, and this is where our mayors and our local leaders are really helping to shape that in their area. So I wouldn’t expect a school to offer all of these, as they don’t offer all GCSEs at the moment. They will specialise in particular areas. If you’re trying to do engineering or construction, for example, you know that involves a lot of problem solving, a lot of maths, a lot of thinking, as well as the hands-on skills that’s required. So it’s not dumbing down, it’s the opposite of that, actually, because this is about raising the standards and the rigour and regulating these qualifications.

headlinePool.title: Russia could attack a Nato country within months, Danish intelligence says
headlinePool.description: Warning comes hours after Poland says fire at Starlink satellite station was ‘act of sabotage’ Russia could launch a limited military attack against a Nato country in the coming months, Danish intelligence said, in one of the starkest warnings yet by western security services. In a report published on Thursday, the Danish defence intelligence service warned of a “low but growing risk” that Russia could launch long-range strikes on Nato infrastructure supporting Ukraine, or carry out a limited incursion into a neighbouring country with a small number of troops, potentially operating without insignia.

headlinePool.title: Mortgage rates have just surpassed 7% for the first time in well over a year
headlinePool.description: Rates have climbed more than a full percentage point since the U.S. war against Iran started.

headlinePool.title: ‘Cracking auction, Gromit!’ Original Aardman puppets go under the hammer
headlinePool.description: Wallace and Gromit stop-motion models and other beloved creations raise money to train new generations of animators Wallace’s reaction as the auction got into full swing might have been a trademark “good grief!” – and the enthusiasm of some of the bidding could have caused even the phlegmatic Gromit to show surprise. Fans of Wallace and Gromit and other beloved creations of the Aardman studio seized the chance to grab souvenirs when more than 200 pieces – including Wallace, Gromit, Shaun the Sheep and Chicken Run puppets that starred in Aardman productions – went under the hammer on Thursday.

headlinePool.title: Poland says fire at Starlink station is sabotage as Denmark warns of rising Russian threat
headlinePool.description: The satellite station is used in part to provide internet coverage to neighbouring Ukraine, the government says.

headlinePool.title: Reported assaults on Great Britain’s railways rise by fifth in a year
headlinePool.description: Unions say record high of nearly 25,000, including assaults on rail workers and public, shows need for more staff and policing The number of reported assaults on Great Britain’s railways has risen by a fifth to a record high of almost 25,000 incidents in a year. Unions said the “horrendous” figures showed the need for more staff and policing, as the Office of Rail and Road (ORR) revealed a sharp increase in assaults on the travelling public and on railway staff last year.

headlinePool.title: At Trump meeting, Xi Jinping lays out terms to avoid US-China military conflict
headlinePool.description: Chinese president’s proposals for lessening tensions come amid period of intense competition between the two countries over AI and trade Trump-Xi summit – latest updates Xi Jingping has called for extensive cooperation with Washington to avoid the “Thucydides trap” that could put the US and China on a military collision course. At the start of his summit meeting with Donald Trump in the White House, the Chinese president laid out terms for a mutual understanding that he said could avoid military conflict between the two competing superpowers.
